To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the combination of the hypervariability regions V1, V2, and V3, and/or V1 and V2, of the 16s rRNA genes were the best molecular marker for distinguishing microbial community patterns from soils under different land management.

LH-PCR is a valuable molecular tool for determining the differences in soil microbial communities and that the combination of three 16S rDNA domains, V1-V3, is an effective tool to distinguish microbial communities from natural and ploughed sagebrush soils.

the combination of three hypervariable 16S rDNA domains (V1, V3, V1+V1+V2) or the combined V2 and V3 domains are the best markers for differentiating microbial community patterns in the same soil type from different land management practices and that Bray-Curtis and multidimensional scaling are better metrics for ordinating and clustering community profiles than the Shannon and Simpson indices.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the use/misuse and the limitations of traditional ecological indices to describe and compare microbial community profiles.
the development of a rapid and sensitive method for assessing microbial community structure in soil.
the use of LH-PCR to distinguish microbial community patterns in soil from the same soil types under different land management regimes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the V1 and V2 domains are the most informative for the study of microbial communities in the soils studied here.
the V1, V2, V3, V5 and V6 hypervariable regions of the 16 S rRNA genes are the best molecular markers to study microbial community patterns.
LH-PCR using the V1, V2, V3 and/or the combined V1+V3 domains is the best method to distinguish between microbial communities in soils under different land management regimes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the V1, V2 and V3 regions of the 16SrRNA gene, or a combination of these, are the most effective regions to use in determining microbial community profiles.
a combination of the V1 and V2 or V1 and V4 domains, or V3 domain alone, would be the most effective for distinguishing the microbial community profiles of these soils.
the use of LH-PCR and a combination of three hypervariable regions, V1, 3, 1+2 is an effective way to determine the microbial diversity of soil communities and to differentiate between soil types.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of traditional ecological indices to measure microbial community diversity is not always the best metric to use when performing metagenomics.
LH-PCR can be a valuable tool to study microbial community structure, but the choice of hypervariable domain(s) is critical for the interpretation and analysis of the data.
the hypervarable domains of the 454 pyrosequenced 16S rDNA gene sequences are useful for determining the differences in microbial community structure in the soils studied.
